<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The `grave-beta-bin.install` file contains a post-install hook that executes a shell script fetched directly from a remote URL using `bash <(curl ...)`. This pattern is a well-known supply-chain attack vector, as it downloads and immediately executes code without integrity verification. The URL points to `gitflic.ru`, a third-party hosting service, and routes through `web.archive.org`, which may obscure the true origin of the script. This setup allows an attacker to modify the script at any time and compromise all users during package installation or upgrade.

Executing unsigned, remotely-hosted scripts in package hooks is not a standard Arch Linux packaging practice and falls outside acceptable risk. Even if the current script appears benign, the lack of checksums or code review enables arbitrary code execution with root privileges. This constitutes a clear backdoor mechanism, as the installed package can run unreviewed, obfuscated, or malicious commands on the target system without user consent.

The use of process substitution (`<(...)`) with `curl` and `bash` is particularly dangerous because it prevents any inspection of the downloaded content before execution. No local file is written for audit, and the command runs in a single pipeline, making it difficult to detect or log the actual payload.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
